facts.fact: The Media Foundation for West Africa describes Mali's 2019 Cybercrime Law as in application, with a National Cybercrime Unit and Court enforcing it.

MFWA says the National Cybercrime Court sentenced editor Youssouf Sissoko in March 2026 to two years and a CFA 1 million fine for 'false information', and the Bamako Court of Appeal sentenced Ras Bath and Rose Vie Chère on 17 August 2026 on charges under information and communication technologies.

MFWA says authorities have systematically used the 2019 Cybercrime Law against journalists, naming cases from November 2024 to June 2026 (Joliba TV guest, Sissoko, Takiou, Keita, Bathily and Doumbia).

MLI.note: Document gives no outage count for Mali's grid.

facts.fact: MFWA says the Bamako Court of Appeal on 17 August 2026 sentenced radio commentator Ras Bath and activist Rose Vie Chère to ten years, three suspended, over broadcast comments on inflation and power outages.

MFWA says editor Abdrahamane Keita was detained by the National Cybercrime Unit on 9 June 2026 after a television appearance and remanded in custody on charges including 'dissemination of false information'.
MFWA says Mali's government formally banned distribution, sale and online circulation of Jeune Afrique in January 2026.

MLI.note: Document names no local digital policy research institution.
